title: Bax Ritter: Shepherd Rescue is live on Android — made with AI art, audio, and code
author: xSyptos
selftext:
Hi, I’m Brandon, the creator of Bax Ritter: Shepherd Rescue. It’s now live on Google Play for Android. The game’s art, audio, and code were created with generative AI, and I used Codex during development.

Two of the practical challenges were screen resizing and tooltips that stayed on screen. The fixed-height canvas was leaving unused space on some screen shapes, including foldable layouts. The current build expands the game view to fill the safe viewport while preserving the artwork’s proportions. Tutorial and action tips now display for six seconds and fade out over one second, with a setting to turn them off. Getting the resized menus, touch targets, and camera to line up was part of that work too.

Bax Ritter is a pixel-art platformer where you play a German shepherd rescuing puppies from a mechanical fortress. You can run, jump, climb, dodge traps, and use Bax’s bark to stun robotic enemies. There are optional puppy rescues, dog tags, and hidden areas to find, plus Endless Mode after the tutorials.

It works offline, supports touch controls and compatible controllers, and has no ads, in-app purchases, or account requirement. Version 1.3.4 has completed Google Play review and is available in production.

Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.syptos.baxritter](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.syptos.baxritter)

For anyone else making mobile games with AI: how are you checking that the game view resizes properly across different screen sizes? I’d also appreciate feedback on Bax Ritter’s controls and readability on your phone.
